keyTakeaways: A teal pumpkin signals a separate container of non-food treats; the house may still give out candy, and that candy carries no allergy promise.
The first teal pumpkin appeared in Knoxville in 2012; FACET spread it to 50 local families in 2013, and FARE took it national in 2014.
On FARE's 2024 map: more than 12,500 homes and venues plus 91 events, spanning every US state, D.C. and 13 further countries including India.
In a Naples sample of 73 allergic children (2026), more than a third (35.6%) had been bullied within two months, and 27.4% blamed it on the allergy.
A child stuck at home can still get a non-food Halloween treat by link: 48.3% of SubhSandesh page views happen on a phone.

faqs.question: Is candy still allowed at a house with a teal pumpkin?
faqs.answer: Yes. FARE's own FAQ says the aim is to add a non-food option, not to take candy away from Halloween. The sweets simply live in a different bowl from the toys.

faqs.question: Is food from a teal pumpkin house allergy-safe?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The teal signal covers only the non-food container; the same household may also offer ordinary candy. Check every food label exactly as you would at an orange-pumpkin house.

faqs.question: Who started the Teal Pumpkin Project, and when?
faqs.answer: Becky Basalone of the Food Allergy Community of East Tennessee painted the first one in 2012, according to a 2014 Kids With Food Allergies interview. Her support group spread it in 2013, and FARE adopted it nationally in 2014.

faqs.question: Is the Teal Pumpkin Project international?
faqs.answer: Yes. FARE reports that its 2024 map reached every US state and Washington, D.C., plus 13 more countries, among them England, Ireland, Scotland, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore and India.

faqs.question: Do I need to paint a real pumpkin to take part?
faqs.answer: No. FARE offers a printable teal pumpkin sign for a door or window, and ready-made teal pumpkins are sold in shops. The sign carries the same meaning as a painted one.

faqs.question: Is there a Teal Pumpkin Project map for 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes. FARE's 2026 Teal Pumpkin Project Map page was live when we looked on 14 October 2026, and both homes and events can be added. Questions go to tealpumpkinproject@foodallergy.org.

faqs.question: Which non-food treats should I leave out of a teal pumpkin bowl?
faqs.answer: FARE flags two traps: some moldable clay contains wheat, and some items contain latex, which a few children react to. Read the pack of anything soft, stretchy or mouldable before adding it.

faqs.question: Which children besides those with food allergies does a teal pumpkin help?
faqs.answer: FARE lists children with food intolerances, eosinophilic oesophagitis, coeliac disease, FPIES, diabetes, feeding tubes, or any special diet. A child fed by tube can use a toy but no sweet at all.

faqs.question: Can a trunk-or-treat car or a school event join in?
faqs.answer: Yes. The very first teal pumpkin decorated an allergist's trunk-or-treat table in 2012, and FARE's 2024 figures count 91 events alongside homes. Keep the non-food container apart from any food on the table.

faqs.question: What time should a teal pumpkin go out?
faqs.answer: Set it out before dusk on 31 October, a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027. If you are adding a map pin, do it a few days earlier so families can plan routes.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Teal Pumpkin Project: What a Teal Pumpkin Means and How to Join

Spotting a teal pumpkin by a front door tells you the household keeps non-food treats, like glow sticks or stickers, in their own container away from the sweets, so an allergic child can pick one without explaining. The Teal Pumpkin Project started with one Knoxville family in 2012 and has been a national programme of the US charity Food Allergy Research & Education, known as FARE, since 2014; its 2024 map listed more than 12,500 locations. For a child who cannot reach your door at all, a Halloween page works as a non-food treat that travels: 48.3% of views of SubhSandesh pages happen on a phone, and creators finish and share 90.9% of what they start.

Below: the origin from its 2014 primary account, four steps to join, who else benefits, the research on exclusion, and the limits. Dates ahead: 31 October lands on a Saturday in 2026 and on a Sunday in 2027.

## What does a teal pumpkin mean?

A teal pumpkin is a doorstep signal that a home offers non-food Halloween treats. It does not mean the house has no candy, and it does not mean the candy is allergy-safe: FARE's own FAQ says households can still hand out sweets, as long as the two kinds of treat sit in separate bowls.

The colour talks so the child need not. FARE runs it under its "Living Teal" campaigns, and its [Teal Pumpkin Project FAQ](https://www.foodallergy.org/resources/about-teal-pumpkin-project) says a printed teal pumpkin sign, taped inside a window or onto the door, carries the same meaning as a painted pumpkin. Read it as a promise about one bowl, not a certificate for the whole house.

## Where the Teal Pumpkin Project came from: Knoxville, 2012 to 2014

The idea began with Becky Basalone, who had recently started the Food Allergy Community of East Tennessee (FACET), a parents' support group. According to an [October 2014 interview published by Kids With Food Allergies](https://community.kidswithfoodallergies.org/blog/spreading-food-allergy-awareness-one-teal-pumpkin-at-a-time), she and her two sons painted a pumpkin teal "two years ago", so in 2012, to decorate their table at an allergist's local trunk-or-treat event.

Back home, her five-year-old set the pumpkin out by the front steps, beside a bowl of leftover non-food items and the usual candy. On Halloween night he held up both bowls and asked visitors whether they wanted "tricks" or "treats", and the tricks, mostly slime and silly glasses, proved the bigger hit.

FACET pushed the idea to its support-group network the following year, 2013, with posters and fliers, and Basalone counted 50 local families in Knoxville. A support-group leader in Georgia then posted the poster on Twitter, where it drew 10,000 hits in a week. [FARE's project page](https://www.foodallergy.org/our-initiatives/awareness-campaigns/living-teal/teal-pumpkin-project) says the charity adopted the initiative nationally in 2014, and it still credits Basalone and FACET.

One correction to the usual retelling: FARE's page names no start year. The 2012 date rests on that 2014 interview, and the first organised campaign ran in 2013. The table sets each stage against the source that records it.

| Period | What happened | Scale | Recorded by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2012 | First teal pumpkin, at an allergist's trunk-or-treat table, then by a Knoxville front door | 1 household, 2 bowls | KFA interview, Oct 2014 |
| 2013 | FACET sends posters and fliers to its network | 50 Knoxville families; 10,000 hits in a week on one tweet | KFA interview, Oct 2014 |
| 2014 | FARE takes the project national with media outreach | Millions saw the media stories, per FACET | FARE project page; KFA interview |
| 2022 to May 2024 | CVS Pharmacy becomes exclusive retail partner (2022); Silver HALO Award, Best Disability Initiative (May 2024) | 1 retail partner, 1 award | FARE project page |
| 2024 | FARE's Teal Pumpkin Project map | 12,500+ locations, 91 events, 50 states + DC, 13 other countries | FARE project page |

A volunteer group carried the project for two seasons before a national charity took it on. The map is now its only countable part.

## How to take part in the Teal Pumpkin Project: 4 steps

FARE's instructions come down to a signal, a non-food bowl and an optional map pin. The steps below keep that order and add the cross-contact care its summary leaves implicit.

### 1. Put out a signal a child can read from the path

- **What:** a painted pumpkin, a shop-bought teal one, or FARE's printable sign in a window.
- **Why:** the family decides before reaching the door, so nobody asks or refuses on the step.
- **Time:** about 2 minutes for a printed sign; an afternoon if paint must dry (our estimate).
- **Source:** FARE's FAQ suggests the sign if you lack time to paint.

### 2. Fill one bowl with checked non-food items only

- **What:** a bowl that never holds food, set up before the first knock.
- **Why:** non-food is not allergen-free. FARE warns that some moldable clay contains wheat and asks for latex-free items.
- **Time:** about 10 minutes to read the packs (our estimate).
- **Source:** FARE Teal Pumpkin Project FAQ.

### 3. Keep food and non-food containers separate all night

- **What:** separate containers in separate spots; clean hands before topping up the non-food bowl.
- **Why:** FARE notes fun-size sweets can differ from full-size bars and some carry no label, so traces travel.
- **Time:** none extra; a second shelf or chair does it.
- **Source:** FARE Teal Pumpkin Project FAQ.

### 4. Add your address or event to the 2026 map, if you are comfortable

- **What:** a pin on FARE's [2026 Teal Pumpkin Project Map](https://www.foodallergy.org/our-initiatives/awareness-campaigns/teal-pumpkin-project/map), live when we looked on 14 October 2026; questions go to tealpumpkinproject@foodallergy.org.
- **Why:** families plan routes from it, and events count as well as homes.
- **Time:** about 5 minutes (our estimate).
- **Source:** FARE map page; FARE's 2024 figures include 91 events.

## Who else a teal pumpkin helps: 7 groups beyond allergy

FARE's FAQ names seven further groups of children for whom candy can be a problem. That is why the project calls itself inclusion rather than allergy awareness alone.

- **Food intolerances:** no anaphylaxis risk, but stomach pain still spoils the night.
- **Eosinophilic oesophagitis (EoE):** a chronic allergic condition of the food pipe, often managed by cutting trigger foods.
- **Coeliac disease:** gluten from wheat, barley or rye damages the gut, and wheat turns up in many sweets.
- **FPIES:** a delayed gut reaction to specific foods, mostly in babies and toddlers.
- **Diabetes:** every sweet has to be counted; a toy needs no arithmetic.
- **Feeding tubes:** some children take nothing by mouth; a toy is the only treat they can use.
- **Any special diet:** medical, religious or family reasons all count.

## Why being left out matters: what 2025 and 2026 research found

FARE says Basalone wanted her son's Halloween to work "without having to refuse candy or disclose his disease at every doorway". Research has since put numbers on what that refusal costs. Researchers in Naples surveyed 73 allergic children, average age 10.6, for a [2026 study in Pediatric Allergy and Immunology](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12900628): over the prior two months 35.6% reported at least one bullying episode, and for 27.4% the allergy itself was the stated motive.

The commonest forms were verbal insults, social exclusion and rumours, and only 60% of affected children told anyone, mostly their parents. In interviews, some described avoiding recess or birthday parties to escape humiliation or exposure, the same retreat a child makes when Halloween turns into a night of saying no.

A [2025 paper in the same journal](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12400901) names this "food allergy-related social anxiety": fear of being judged for declining offered food, separate from fear of a reaction. Its authors describe how skipping a party to dodge the awkwardness reinforces the fear next time. Our inference, not theirs: a door where the child simply picks a toy removes one of those moments.

## The limits: what a teal pumpkin does not promise

The commonest misreading is that teal means "safe food here", and one local-news page in the current results says exactly that. FARE's FAQ says the opposite: a teal house may still offer candy from a second bowl, so read every label as you would anywhere.

A non-food bowl is not automatically allergen-free either, and one refilled by a hand that has just unwrapped chocolate can carry traces. The signal is only as good as the person keeping the bowls apart.

Coverage is thin. Some 12,500 map locations in 2024, across 14 countries, is small next to every street out trick-or-treating, so most children pass far more orange pumpkins than teal ones. The map is also public: a home pin shows your address to anyone, and 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators lock their own pages with a password, so a family wary of strangers may prefer a window sign with no pin.

## A non-food treat for the child who cannot come to your door

Some children cannot trick-or-treat at all: they are in hospital, recovering, or living in another city. For them a Halloween page sent to a parent's phone is a treat with nothing to eat in it, and since 48.3% of SubhSandesh page views come from phones, that is where a parent will most likely see it.

The [Halloween photo card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is the quick option, around five minutes of work: up to six pictures, a pumpkin the child carves to reveal a word you pick, and a Kids mode drawn with round, blushing ghosts and no blood or sudden frights. The [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) suits a grandparent with more to say: a voice message of up to a minute, room for 12 pictures, an optional time lock with a countdown, and one written reply that comes back to you; its family and kids settings drop the No button entirely.

Each page greets one person, it is not built for parties, and neither replaces a teal bowl on the night. If a Halloween theme is wrong, [see the full SubhSandesh template list](https://subhsandesh.in/templates); if the child is at your door, a glow stick beats any link.

auditReport.honestAssessment: It is the only page in the top 10 that dates the origin from a 2014 primary account and corrects the '2012 founding' shorthand, prints FARE's 2024 map scale, says plainly that teal does not certify food (a ranking local-news page says the opposite), and cites peer-reviewed 2025-2026 research on food-allergy exclusion. CSPI and FARE itself carry far more authority on this term, so expect this to compete for 'teal pumpkin meaning' and AI-answer citations on the origin and limits, not for the head term.
